description: Human-readable Solidity rule definitions aligned with smartgraphical/adapters/solidity/adapter.py (build_rule_registry). Machine-readable checklist: tests/fixtures/solidity_task_coverage.json.
readme_source: README.md (section SmartGraphical checks the Solidity tasks below)

notes.task_12: CLI/API task 12 is graph visualization only; no RuleSpec entry in build_rule_registry().
notes.meta_all: Task 13 / 'all' runs tasks 1-11 plus 14 then graph; see adapter and API docs.

rules.title: Old Version Markers
rules.remediation_hint: Review rewrite markers and keep comments aligned with the current implementation.
rules.rationale: After a rewrite or upgrade, stale comments about versions or signatures can mislead maintainers and hide logical mismatches between documentation and behavior (README Task 1).
rules.detection_logic: Flag comments that contain loose keywords such as ' version ', ' new ', or ' old ' as possible rewrite drift markers.
false_positive_patterns: Comments that legitimately describe versioning without implying a stale contract migration.
Narrative text in NatSpec that uses the same words in a non-signature context.

rules.title: External State Manipulation
rules.remediation_hint: Check assignments sourced from inputs or external values before they update sensitive state.
rules.rationale: Parameters or reads from other contracts can change between calls; mutating totals, balances, or fees using that data without guards risks inconsistent state (README Tasks 2 and shared themes with 4/5/9).
rules.detection_logic: Heuristic: assignments touching names like totalSupply, balance, fee, supply, or amount without a require on the same statement; normalized path skips guarded or permissioned entrypoints.
false_positive_patterns: Assignments already conditioned on require/assert or admin-only modifiers.
Renamed variables that no longer represent economic state.

rules.title: Stake And Release Logic
rules.remediation_hint: Verify that stake and release paths are symmetric and guard the manipulated amount.
rules.rationale: Collateral and staking flows must stay balanced; mistakes in release, caps, or encumbrance windows enable over-withdrawal or duplicate borrowing style issues (README Task 3 and joint note with 5/9).
rules.detection_logic: Surface functions or bodies mentioning stake/unstake tokens for manual review of symmetric accounting and guards.
false_positive_patterns: Narrow helper names that contain 'stake' but are view-only or unrelated to collateral.
Libraries that wrap staking without holding funds in the same contract.

rules.title: Pool Supply Operations
rules.remediation_hint: Review mint or burn style flows for missing access control and accounting assumptions.
rules.rationale: Mint and burn change supply; external entrypoints without access control or unclear conditions can desynchronize pool accounting (README Tasks 2 and 4).
rules.detection_logic: Flag external mint/burn functions lacking only* style modifiers; emit conditions and zero-address burns in mint/burn bodies for review; normalized path flags external mint/burn without permissions.
false_positive_patterns: Intentionally public mint with upstream factory gate.
Burn-to-dead-address patterns that are documented and guarded elsewhere.

rules.title: Local Incentive Accounting
rules.remediation_hint: Confirm that earning and spending paths validate the tracked balance or allowance state.
rules.rationale: Point or token economies need consistent earn vs spend checks; spending without proving prior earning breaks incentive logic (README Tasks 2, 5, 9).
rules.detection_logic: Functions whose names suggest receive/take/burn/point flows but lack require lines referencing allowance, balance, or point state when those names exist on the contract.
false_positive_patterns: Off-chain credited systems with different naming.
Internal functions that inherit checks from callers.

rules.title: Error Path Consistency
rules.remediation_hint: Inspect try/catch handlers and ensure the error path preserves valid state transitions.
rules.rationale: Incorrect try/catch recovery can leave state inconsistent or replayable after external failures (README Task 6).
rules.detection_logic: Parse try/catch blocks for empty catches, missing reverts, or assert misuse that may swallow faults.
false_positive_patterns: Deliberate no-op catches with documented compensating actions elsewhere.
Test-only fixtures with simplified error handling.

rules.title: Complicated Calculations
rules.remediation_hint: Review arithmetic-heavy expressions and simplify or guard the most complex branches.
rules.rationale: Dense math expands the attack surface for rounding, overflow, and branch-specific manipulation (README Task 7).
rules.detection_logic: Flag statements combining mul/div (SafeMath style or operators), bare division, math.* helpers, or nested parentheses with arithmetic ops in normalized computation spans.
false_positive_patterns: Fixed-precision libraries with audited rounding.
Comments or strings that mention .div without executable code.

rules.title: Sensitive Call Ordering
rules.remediation_hint: Check whether fetch, price, or preparation logic happens immediately before transfer-like effects.
rules.rationale: Oracle or price reads must stay adjacent to transfers; stale reads enable manipulation (README Tasks 8 and 9).
rules.detection_logic: When functions mention transfer/withdraw/unstake, require earlier statements in the same body that reference rebase/fetch style preparation markers before the effect.
false_positive_patterns: Internal helpers that already synchronized price and state.
Patterns using separate modifiers for ordering guarantees.

rules.title: Withdraw Preconditions
rules.remediation_hint: Ensure withdraw-style operations are preceded by guards, conditions, or validated system checks.
rules.rationale: Withdrawals without pre-checks can violate entitlement invariants, especially when value entered via staking or deposits (README Tasks 3, 5, 8, 9).
rules.detection_logic: For withdraw/unstake/transfer callees, flag statement slices lacking require coverage while skipping systematic helper names (transfers, approvals, fee managers, verify helpers).
false_positive_patterns: Withdrawals gated by modifiers instead of inline require.
Routed calls where validation happens in nested internal functions.

rules.title: Similar Names
rules.remediation_hint: Rename near-duplicate identifiers when they can confuse reviewers or callers.
rules.rationale: Near-duplicate names invite mistaken wiring and hard-to-spot substitutions in review or exploit paths (README Task 10).
rules.detection_logic: Similarity heuristics across function and variable identifiers within a contract to surface likely collisions.
false_positive_patterns: Intentional paired names in upgrade hooks with clear documentation.
Generated getters that must mirror EIP interfaces.

rules.title: Outer Calls
rules.remediation_hint: Review public entrypoints that consume inputs and mutate state without stronger constraints.
rules.rationale: Fully public functions that accept inputs and mutate inventory or state need extra scrutiny for access and validation (README Task 11).
rules.detection_logic: External entrypoints with parameters used in mutations but without require, permission modifiers, or early returns; skips high centrality helpers already reviewed intra-contract.
false_positive_patterns: Trusted forwarder or meta-tx entry with upstream authorization.
Router contracts designed as permissionless aggregators.

rules.title: Minimum Bounds On Swap And Liquidity Calls
rules.remediation_hint: Replace zero literals for min-amount, min-shares, and deadline parameters with user-supplied or quote-derived bounds.
rules.rationale: DEX and pool integrations should not pass zero or false bounds where callers expect slippage or deadline protection; missing bounds enable sandwiching and unfavorable execution.
rules.detection_logic: On function_to_function edges, flag literal 0 or false for formal parameters whose names hint min-out, max-in, deadline, or sqrt price limits on swap or liquidity callees.
false_positive_patterns: Internal test doubles or mocks with deliberate zero bounds.
Custom routers that rename parameters outside the substring heuristics.
